name: West Spitsbergen Current
scope: OSW reference corridor from a selected Barents Sea opening northward-departure approach at 73 N, west of Bear Island and Svalbard, to a selected pre-branching gate near 79.6 N. Excludes upstream Norwegian Atlantic routes, eastward Barents inflow, offshore Front Current feeder, westward recirculation, shelf/fjord intrusions and downstream Svalbard/Yermak/Yermak Pass branches. No whole connected Arctic pathway length.
layer: Atlantic-water boundary-flow naming context, with upper-slope and lower-slope components distinguished in source. Menze et al. mapped 20-500 m depth-averaged summer flow near the northern branch region; no depth-specific axis or uniform full-width footprint reconstructed.
time_convention: Regional geography from 2018/2019 papers. Northern pathway observations span summers 2014-2017; this selected approach route is not a dated summer track, annual mean axis or seasonal geometry.
source_locator: Introduction and Figure 1: Atlantic flow splits between Scandinavia and Svalbard into Barents inflow via Bear Island Trough and northward WSC continuation; shelf/slope components differ.
source_citation: Goszczko, Ingvaldsen and Onarheim (2018), Wind-Driven Cross-Shelf Exchange—West Spitsbergen Current as a Source of Heat and Salt for the Adjacent Shelf in Arctic Winters, JGR Oceans, doi:10.1002/2017JC013553.

supporting_sources.citation: Menze et al. (2019), Atlantic Water Pathways Along the North-Western Svalbard Shelf Mapped Using Vessel-Mounted Current Profilers, JGR Oceans, doi:10.1029/2018JC014299.
supporting_sources.locator: Abstract; sections 4.3 and 6: northward boundary flow at 79-80 N / 5-10 E, splitting into Svalbard, Yermak and Yermak Pass branches.
supporting_sources.role: Northern branch-region context; summer composite does not establish all branches at every time.

supporting_sources.role: Source-specific naming and section/season caveats; transect distances are not current length or width.

coordinate_selection: Every vertex is OSW-selected. Source describes regional bifurcation, not a 73 N exact origin; selected 72.5/73/73.5 N approaches test departure naming. Northern 79.5-79.8 N gates stop within the branch region. Longitudes and bends are editorial; no bathymetric contour, source arrow, velocity field or track digitized.
